prompt: A metal has a density of $7.8$ grams per cubic centimeter. What is the mass, in grams, of a $250$ cubic centimeter block of this metal?
hint: Density is mass per unit volume, so mass is density times volume.

hints.text: Density is mass per unit volume, so mass is density times volume.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try round numbers: at $2$ g per cm³, a $10$ cm³ block weighs $20$ g — you multiply. Density times volume gives mass, and the cm³ units cancel to confirm it.

learningObjective: Apply a density rate to compute a total.
explanation: $7.8 \dfrac{\text{g}}{\text{cm}^3} \times 250 \text{ cm}^3 = 1950$ grams — the cubic centimeters cancel, leaving grams ✓
Dividing instead would give about $32$, which is not a plausible mass for a block of metal.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate to check the magnitude
steps: The exact answer of $1950$ sits just below that, exactly as expected.
A five-second estimate catches an order-of-magnitude error, which is the kind that costs a whole question.
